skill.name: run-tests
skill.description: Guides an AI assistant to run project tests, targeted test files, affected tests, coverage, and failed-test debugging.
skill.summary: Run project tests, focused test files, affected tests, and coverage checks.
skill.author: Clouder0

security_audit.summary: The static findings are Markdown backticks and code fences, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The skill still uses Bash test commands, and the file placeholder on line 23 needs quoting guidance to reduce command injection risk. No evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unquoted file placeholder in a Bash test command
remediation.suggestion: Document that file paths must be quoted or passed as safe arguments before replacing the placeholder. Reject paths that contain shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: Generic project test scripts may run arbitrary package commands
remediation.suggestion: Advise users to review the project test script before running this skill in an untrusted repository.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged backticks are Markdown code-fence delimiters, not Ruby command-substitution syntax. The fenced block documents test commands and contains no backtick evaluation logic.
Line 28 is only the closing Markdown code fence for the test-command example. It is not executable Ruby or shell backtick syntax.
The backticks format glob examples in Markdown. They do not execute shell commands or evaluate dynamic input.
The backticks format a test naming example in Markdown. This is documentation text, not command execution syntax.
The flagged text is a Markdown code fence around a fixed coverage command. It is not Ruby backtick execution; the general Bash risk is handled separately.

semantic_findings.title: Unquoted File Placeholder in Test Command
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md shows `npm test -- --testPathPattern={file}` without quoting or validation guidance. If an agent substitutes an untrusted path into Bash, shell metacharacters could alter the command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The placeholder is in a Bash command and is intended for file-specific test runs. Exploitation depends on untrusted path substitution, so confidence is moderate.

content.value_statement: Developers need a consistent way to verify code changes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code project-specific test commands.
actual_capabilities: Runs the default npm test command for the project.
Runs a specific test file using a testPathPattern placeholder.
Runs tests changed since HEAD with npm test arguments.
Runs coverage with npm test coverage arguments.
Guides failed-test debugging with a short checklist.
limitations: Only npm examples are active commands; pytest, Go, and Cargo examples are comments.
Requires the project to define a working npm test script.
Does not detect the correct test framework automatically.
File path placeholders need careful quoting before Bash execution.

use_cases.title: Verify a Code Change
use_cases.description: Run the full project test suite before merging or sharing a change.

use_cases.title: Check Focused Test Failures
use_cases.description: Run a single test file and inspect failures before broader validation.

use_cases.title: Confirm Assistant Work
use_cases.description: Ask an AI coding assistant to run tests after implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Run All Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification after a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the run-tests skill to run the full project test suite and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run One Test File
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused check for a changed test file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the run-tests skill to run the tests for this file: <path>. Quote the path safely before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Run Affected Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Medium confidence check before a commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the run-tests skill to run tests affected by changes since HEAD. Report failures with likely next files to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Run Coverage and Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the run-tests skill to run coverage, identify any failing tests, and propose a minimal follow-up test plan.

output_examples.input: Run all tests before I commit this change.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs the full test suite, reports pass or fail, and summarizes any failed suites with next debugging steps.

output_examples.input: Run the tests for one changed file.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs a focused test command for the provided file path and explains whether broader testing is still needed.
The assistant runs coverage mode, reports the overall result, and highlights test areas that need attention.

best_practices: Run the full suite before publishing or merging changes.
Quote file paths when replacing placeholders in Bash commands.
Read failure messages before editing tests or source files.
anti_patterns: Do not paste untrusted file names into shell commands without quoting.
Do not assume commented framework examples are enabled.
Do not ignore failing tests after a targeted run passes.

faq.question: What test runner does this skill use?
faq.answer: The active commands use npm test. Other framework examples are included only as comments.

faq.question: Can it run a single test file?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a file-specific test pattern that should be used with a safely quoted path.

faq.question: Does it run coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a coverage command using npm test coverage arguments.

faq.question: Does it choose the right framework automatically?
faq.answer: No. The user or assistant must confirm that the project uses the documented npm test workflow.

faq.question: Is it safe in untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Project test scripts can run arbitrary package commands, so review scripts first.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
